title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
description: A long return becomes a meditation on memory, disguise, hospitality, and the shape of home.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
description: Anger opens into a study of mortality, honour, and compassion.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
description: A dialogue that moves from justice in a person to how a city should be shaped.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: Private notes on discipline, impermanence, and meeting the present moment.

title: The Dhammapada
author: Traditionally attributed to the Buddha
description: Verses on attention, compassion, desire, and the path beyond suffering.

title: The Bible
author: Many authors and traditions
description: A library of law, poetry, prophecy, wisdom, gospel, and letters in conversation.

title: Confessions
author: Augustine of Hippo
description: A life told as a prayer, asking how desire, time, memory, and grace make a self.

title: The Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
description: The afterlife becomes an architecture of ethics, politics, love, and poetic language.

title: Essays
author: Michel de Montaigne
description: An open form for testing habit, education, friendship, death, and certainty.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: A reader turns life into chivalric fiction, and the world answers with comedy and tenderness.

title: Faust
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
description: A scholar’s bargain opens into a drama about knowledge, desire, power, and meaning.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: A philosophical poem asking how to create values after old certainties fall away.

title: In Search of Lost Time
author: Marcel Proust
description: A life is recovered through involuntary memory, social observation, jealousy, and art.

title: The Trial
author: Franz Kafka
description: An arrest without an explanation turns the ordinary world into an opaque machine of judgment.

title: The Waste Land
author: T. S. Eliot
description: Voices, myths, cities, and languages break apart while searching for renewal.

title: Being and Nothingness
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
description: Consciousness, bad faith, and freedom meet in an account of self-making.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: The Buendía family’s repeated histories turn one town into a study of memory and solitude.
